deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a methodological and physiological passage from Riemann's drafts for 'Mechanik des Ohres' (published posthumously by Henle in 1867). The argument runs as follows.

(1) Continuing from the previous page, the ossicles may be held in their correct position by several possible agents: muscles, joint capsules, ligaments, mucous folds and membranes. Choosing the most probable mechanism would require anatomical study of fresh specimens, to estimate the elasticity and tension of the ligaments and membranes. Riemann says this is impossible for him. He hopes instead that carefully comparing what each hypothesis achieves will expose improbabilities in some of them, so that they can be dismissed.

(2) He introduces a working distinction between the 'listening' ear ('lauschendes Ohr'), adapted for exact hearing, and the non-listening ear. For certain questions he adds a second distinction, apparently between the ear of the newborn and that of the adult.

(3) Definition: the ear is 'listening' when the tensor tympani muscle pulls the stapes footplate slightly inward against the labyrinth fluid. The pressure in the labyrinth fluid is then slightly greater than the air pressure in the tympanic cavity, and the links of the ossicular chain are pressed slightly against one another, so the chain stays closed.

(4) He considers an objection. Some may think such a permanent tension (the tympanic membrane perhaps excepted) improbable. Their reason would be that the ossicles can change position without being pressed together, through the ligaments and joints and through gradual changes in muscle contraction.

(5) Conclusion: suppose we have found that exact hearing is secured only when all parts of the apparatus engage with one another. Then the analysis certainly holds for the listening ear. It remains possible that the human ear is adapted permanently, perhaps only slightly.

The only quantitative content is qualitative: p_labyrinth slightly greater than p_tympanum in the listening state. Nothing beyond this is supplied.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics. The physiological premise is outdated as stated. Modern physiology sees the tensor tympani mainly as damping and protective (as in the acoustic reflex). It is not usually seen as maintaining a constant preload for exact hearing. Riemann himself leaves open whether the adaptation is permanent.

results.what: Distinction between the 'listening' (adapted) ear and the non-listening ear. The listening state is defined by the tensor tympani pressing the stapes footplate inward, so that labyrinth pressure slightly exceeds tympanic air pressure and the ossicular chain stays closed under slight compression.
results.modern_name: Accommodation / preload of the ossicular chain by the middle-ear muscles; role of the tensor tympani
results.usually_credited_to: Discussed in the 1860s by Helmholtz (Mechanik der Gehörknöchelchen, 1868), Johannes Müller, Toynbee and Politzer; Riemann's version appears in his posthumous 'Mechanik des Ohres' (1867)

results.what: Methodological remark: when anatomical data on ligament elasticity are unavailable, competing hypotheses about how ossicle position is regulated should be compared to expose improbabilities.
results.modern_name: Hypothesis elimination / inverse ('synthetic') method in physiology
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's own methodological introduction to 'Mechanik des Ohres' (the following page of this bundle)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely verbal physiological discussion. It is a draft of material that appears in Riemann's posthumously published 'Mechanik des Ohres' (1867). It contains no mathematics and nothing not already associated with him.
transcription_corrections: 'Man darf jedoch wünschen[?]' probably reads 'Man darf jedoch hoffen, durch sorgfältige Vergleichung ...'.
'zwischen dem Ohr des Hören-den[?] und des Erwachsenen' more plausibly reads 'zwischen dem Ohr des Neuge-borenen und des Erwachsenen' (line-break hyphenation); uncertain.

'Wir nennen[?] die Unterscheidung' is probably 'Wir machen die Unterscheidung' (or the start of a definition, 'Wir nennen das Ohr lauschend, wenn ...'); 'nennen die Unterscheidung' is not grammatical.
'Wird[?] wir gefunden haben' should read 'Wenn wir gefunden haben, dass nur dann das genaue Hören ...'.
'durch die Stellung des Hammer[?] und Ambosgelenks[?]' may read 'durch die Wirkung der Haft- und Gelenkbänder'; uncertain.
'Contracturen[?] der Muskeln' is more likely 'Contraction(en) der Muskeln'.
'bei der Zahl[?] der Fälle[?]' is uncertain; possibly 'bei der Erklärung der Thatsachen'.
'genauen Hören erblich[?]' is doubtful; the inserted word above the struck-out one is unclear (possibly 'ausschliesslich' or 'vorzugsweise').
